success_patterns: Every success had the clue's distinctive wording echoed in the passages: archive lines ('Golden Boy playwright... Poker Man's Polo', 'sexiest murderesses... 1996, CHICAGO'), a dictionary definition ('The portion of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line' -> Homestretch), or a rules sentence ('A ringer scores three points'). The agent took the term attached to that echo instead of overthinking.
For definition-style clues with no 'this', the answer was the headword or term. The passage titles ('Homestretch - definition of...') and the sentence restating the clue's numbers gave it.

The agent answered with the right slot type: the larger container (state, not county), the title character (Anastasia, not the actress), the playwright rather than the play, the detective rather than the story.

When passages gave spelling or form variants (Casimir/Kazimierz Pulaski, 'Chicago (musical)'), the agent chose the plain English form used in the passage that echoed the clue, without Wikipedia disambiguators.

patch.reasoning: Eight easy passes share one mechanism: find the passage that restates the clue and take the term attached to it. Rule 3 covers archive lines and slot-blank sentences but not plain dictionary-definition or rules-sentence clues with no 'this'. It also says nothing about choosing among spelling variants or stripping disambiguators. Earlier epochs rejected heavy mandatory-template edits, so these are two short additions to existing sections with no new top-level structure and no change to the protected block.

edits.target: - Archive lines may also be formatted 'CATEGORY | clue text | answer'. Take the answer that follows the clue, even if the whole context is one short passage.
edits.content: - DEFINITION / RULES CLUES ('It's the part of a racetrack from the last turn to the finish line', '3 points on one throw in horseshoes'): the clue is a definition, so the answer is the TERM being defined. Find the passage that restates the definition (dictionary entry, glossary, rules page, 'X: the portion of...', 'A ringer scores three points'). The term is its headword, the word in the passage titles ('Homestretch - definition of...'), or the word the sentence attaches to the same numbers. Answer with that single term, not a paraphrase and not a longer phrase.

edits.target: - Honor qualifiers when the context offers several names for the same thing: 'Greek god of erotic love' -> 'Eros' (not Roman 'Cupid').
edits.content: - When passages give variant spellings or forms of the same answer (Casimir vs Kazimierz Pulaski, 'Chicago (musical)', 'Anastasia (1956 film)'), use the plain English form that the clue-echoing passage and most titles use. Drop Wikipedia-style disambiguators in parentheses. Choose the entity the clue's other facts point to (the title character, the larger state, the creator) and ignore the actor, county or work named beside it.
